description:
One action a Heinzelmännchen reports: who, when, which verb, on what; metadata only, never content.

Verb-specific fields: `read` may carry the `version` read and `needed_by`, when the reader's contract needs it;
`drafted` the `contract_version` it drafted from; `approved` who approved it (`by`); `published` the `version`
published; `fell_back` the stale `input` it used. `heartbeat` has no target. `part` names the part of the target
the action concerns, e.g. the row of a tracker one person keeps.

heinzel_id.description: The Heinzelmännchen's id: a slug, unique in your team, e.g. `costas-tracker`; it becomes the durable id of a Heinzelmännchen once those exist.
heinzel_id.title: Heinzel Id

user.description: Its user's handle in the team's roster.
user.title: User

time.description: When it happened, with its offset; stored in UTC.
time.title: Time

verb.description: What it did: read, drafted, approved, published, fell_back or heartbeat.
verb.title: Verb

target.description: What it acted on: an https URL (no user name, password or credential in it), an email address published to, a team contract's output as `contract:team/<name>#<output>`, or a chat channel as `chat:<channel>`. None only for a heartbeat.
target.title: Target

description.description: What a reader of the graph should know, in one line; never content, names or addresses.
description.title: Description

contract.description: The team contract the action keeps, `team:<name>`; personal contracts never appear here.
contract.title: Contract

part.description: The part of the target it concerns, e.g. a tracker's row.
part.title: Part

version.description: The artifact's version read or published, as its source has it.
version.title: Version

needed_by.description: For `read`: by when the reader's contract needs the artifact.
needed_by.title: Needed By

input.description: For `fell_back`: the input whose stale version it used.
input.title: Input

title: One entry of a Heinzelmännchen's telemetry log
